subject: Vendor onboarding: invoice routing choices + non-standard line items
messages:
From: Accounts AR - Nimbus Supply <accounts@nimbussupply.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: New vendor onboarding — invoice routing & a couple of odd line item types

Hi Ethan,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call this morning. Two quick follow-ups from our side as we get ready to submit our first invoice:

1) Portal vs. email — is Redwood's vendor portal required for all invoices going forward, or can we fall back to sending to AP email (accounts-payable@redwood.com) when a PDF/CVS is generated by our ERP? We have a handful of invoices that include mixed charge types and an attached CSV for line-item reconciliation; curious if the portal supports CSV attachments and line-item mapping.

2) Non-standard line items — we sometimes send credit adjustments and one-time freight surcharges as separate line types that don't map cleanly to a single PO line. Do you have guidance on how to represent those in the portal template? If the portal can't, we may need an email fallback with a clear subject token so your system can auto-route.

I attached a sanitized sample invoice and CSV extract (nimbus_sample_invoice.csv) showing the two unusual rows. If you prefer, we can also start by emailing a PDF until portal mapping is confirmed.

Next steps from us: hold off on any invoice submission until we hear your preference.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Billing Lead, Nimbus Supply
accounts@nimbussupply.com
[attachment: nimbus_sample_invoice.csv (CSV)]

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
To: Accounts AR - Nimbus Supply <accounts@nimbussupply.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New vendor onboarding — invoice routing & a couple of odd line item types

Hi Liam — great to meet earlier. Short answers up front:

- Preferred path: vendor portal. It gives the fastest ACK and preserves PO-line mapping.
- Email fallback: supported, but must include the PO number in the subject and we rely on an "AP:PO=<po-number>" token for automated routing.
- CSV/line item support: portal accepts CSV line-item attachments (see sample mapping below). For the odd types you described (credit adjustments, freight surcharges), use the following pattern so our ingest normalizes correctly:

Portal CSV columns we expect: po_number, line_number, item_description, quantity, unit_price, tax_code, charge_type
- charge_type values: standard | credit_adjustment | surcharge
- For credit_adjustment, include a negative quantity or unit_price and set charge_type=credit_adjustment.
- For one-time freight, set charge_type=surcharge and include related_po in notes if it applies to multiple POs.

If you must send by email (short-term), subject line must include: "AP:PO=<po-number> Vendor:Nimbus" and attach either PDF+CSV zipped or a single CSV. We'll auto-ingest if formatted as above. Otherwise the invoice will go to manual review and could delay payment.

I've attached our standard onboarding form and a quick mapping example. 

Best,
Ethan Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ethan — that's helpful. Two clarifying questions from our billing team: 

1) PO formatting — do you require the PO prefix (e.g., "RDW-") or just the numeric ID? Our ERP exports without prefixes. Will the ingest accept both variants?

2) Multiple charges on single invoice — if we have 3 different PO lines plus a consolidated freight surcharge that relates to the whole invoice, do you prefer (A) adding that surcharge as a separate CSV line with charge_type=surcharge and no PO (use blank PO + note), or (B) attach a small reconciliation file that maps the surcharge to individual PO numbers?

We'll prepare a test CSV and push it through the portal tomorrow morning; if you want to watch the ingestion we can hold on submitting to production.

—Liam
